# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

import base64
import json
import os

import sys

import time

# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa

# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached..."). We could make the roles classifier match the rate-limit INSIDE the exhaustion story. Hmm, but issue #1168 explicitly made the exhaustion terminal opaque to prevent re-classification ("treat the signature as terminal - no further retries, no 'not retried' rewrap"). But that's for the transport class. Actually `isTransientExhaustionStory` is excluded from `isTransientTransportError` — but `isRateLimitOrQuota` doesn't check the exhaustion signature; it only matches patterns. So a rate-limit-ladder exhaustion ("Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 60s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...") WOULD match `rate.?limit` patterns via the attempts evidence → `isRateLimitOrQuota` returns true → the roles layer WOULD rotate/fail over. Interesting! That actually composes: the inner ladder does a few quick in-place retries with backoff; on exhaustion, the roles layer sees a rate-limit-shaped terminal and rotates/fails over.

Hmm wait, but that means for roles-configured setups, a 429 now: entry-1 provider ladder retries up to its budget (with backoff honoring Retry-After) before roles rotate. That changes timing but keeps semantics: rotation still happens, just later. But omp's policy "free credential switch first" would be delayed... And existing roles tests: they test with fake stream functions, not real provider adapters — the FallbackStreamFunction tests inject their own `streamForKey` (which don't include the transient wrapper). So roles tests wouldn't break.

But is it GOOD? A rate-limited key with 3 chain entries: inner ladder burns, say, 3 attempts × backoff (min 2s max 60s each) before failover. With `Retry-After: 60`, that's ~2 minutes wasted before rotating to a working key. Bad for multi-key setups. But the harbor bench scenario (single key, single model) is the primary target.

**Option B (wire the roles engine even for a single model):** Make the CLI wrap the legacy stream in a single-entry FallbackStreamFunction. This gives 429 retries with backoff, honoring Retry-After, plus the last-entry wait-out (`maxWaitForLastEntry`). But: FallbackStreamFunction needs ChainEntry with keyRing and streamForKey; constructing from the legacy path requires plumbing. And it changes a LOT of behavior for single-model users (notices, cooldowns, exhaustion stories). Bigger blast radius. Also the ticket explicitly says "In fa's provider layer".

**Option C (bounded 429 retry in the transient ladder, opt-out when roles exist):** In `providerStreamFunction`, we don't know whether a roles wrapper will sit above. But actually — does it matter? Roles wrapper sits above ONLY when roles resolve. The provider functions are also used directly by compaction smol streams etc.

Let me re-read the ticket's proposed fix:

"In fa's provider layer: classify 429/5xx/timeouts as transient → retry with exponential backoff + jitter (e.g., min 2s, max 60s, honoring Retry-After), bounded by the deadline clock (leave the 120s wrap-up margin intact). 401/403/400 stay fatal."

So the ticket wants the provider-layer ladder to treat 429 like other transient errors — retry in place with backoff, honoring Retry-After, bounded by deadline. The "429_retry event to the session log" for post-mortems.

The order differs slightly but the outcome class is preserved.

## Design

### 1. Provider-layer rate-limit retry (`transient_retry_stream.dart`)

Add a rate-limit retry class to the transient ladder:

- Classification: `isRateLimitError(AssistantMessage)` — reuses the existing `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` (already in this file) — message stopReason error, not overflow, not budget exhaustion (budget exhaustion must NOT retry — issue #926; `isBudgetExhaustion` check already excludes it in `isTransientNetworkError`... wait, for rate limit classification I need to make sure budget exhaustion ("spending limit reached") doesn't classify as retryable rate limit. `isBudgetExhaustion` check must come first).

- Retry policy: exponential backoff + jitter: `min 2s, max 60s` per ticket; honoring `Retry-After` when the event carries it; attempts budget separate from the transport budget (e.g., 5 attempts total per call? The ticket says "min 2s, max 60s" for the delay, bounded by the deadline). Let me define: `maxRateLimitAttempts = 5`? Hmm. With 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s (+jitter) — total ~62s+Retry-After waits. Reasonable for a transient quota blip. Actually since we honor Retry-After, a `Retry-After: 30` gives delays 30, 60(capped)... Let me keep the default transport budget untouched (maxAttempts=3, 5s) and add a rate-limit ladder with its own budget.

- Deadline bound: before sleeping, check the deadline seam: `transientRetryDeadlineLeft()` — returns remaining ms on the session deadline, or null. If the wait (delay + wrap-up margin) exceeds the remaining time → stop retrying, push the exhaustion terminal. "leave the 120s wrap-up margin intact": the wrap-up margin is 120s in the harbor context (the adapter already subtracts 120s when exporting FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS — so fa's deadline ALREADY has the margin baked in). Hmm wait, re-read: "a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin)". So fa's armed deadline already includes the 120s margin — fa's deadline fires 120s before the real guillotine. So the provider ladder bounded by fa's deadline inherently leaves the wrap-up margin intact. 

So the bound: never sleep past the deadline; if `now + delay >= deadline`, stop retrying. Also cap the delay at min(60s, remaining - margin)? The margin inside fa: `deadlineEpochMs` is the deadline; the ladder should keep some margin for the wrap-up answer to land — the ticket says "never retries past the wrap-up margin". The wrap-up margin inside fa is the deadline ladder's wrapUpSteerMs (3 min default)... Hmm, but that's for steering. For the retry ladder, simplest correct interpretation: 
  - retry while: attempts remain AND the next delay would end before (deadline - safety margin), where safety margin = 120s default (the same margin the adapter uses).

Hmm wait, but then with the harbor-exported deadline (already cap - 120s), retrying until (deadline - 120s) leaves 240s before the real guillotine. That's fine and safe.

But careful: what if the deadline is NOT armed (interactive CLI runs)? Then no deadline bound — just the attempts budget. Good: interactive users get retries too (that's desirable).

Let me define the seam to inject the deadline + clock for tests:
- `int? Function()? transientRetryDeadlineMs` — global, returns the armed deadline epoch-ms or null (null = unbounded). 
- Clock: reuse `DateTime.now()`... better inject via a global `DateTime Function()? transientRetryClock`? The existing ladder doesn't have a clock seam but reports elapsed via DateTime.now(). For testability, keep the deadline seam returning remaining-ms directly: `Duration? Function()? transientRetryDeadlineLeft` — returns remaining time or null. Then tests inject a mutable closure; no clock needed for the deadline logic (each call re-evaluates). That's clean and avoids clock injection in the ladder.

Wire-up: in `AgentCli` (agent_cli.dart), where `_deadline` exists, set `transientRetryDeadlineLeft = _deadline.isArmed ? () => Duration(milliseconds: _deadline.remainingMs) : null`. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of

  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native

  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the

fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`

Usage:

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached..."). We could make the roles classifier match the rate-limit INSIDE the exhaustion story. Hmm, but issue #1168 explicitly made the exhaustion terminal opaque to prevent re-classification ("treat the signature as terminal - no further retries, no 'not retried' rewrap"). But that's for the transport class. Actually `isTransientExhaustionStory` is excluded from `isTransientTransportError` — but `isRateLimitOrQuota` doesn't check the exhaustion signature; it only matches patterns. So a rate-limit-ladder exhaustion ("Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 60s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...") WOULD match `rate.?limit` patterns via the attempts evidence → `isRateLimitOrQuota` returns true → the roles layer WOULD rotate/fail over. Interesting! That actually composes: the inner ladder does a few quick in-place retries with backoff; on exhaustion, the roles layer sees a rate-limit-shaped terminal and rotates/fails over.

Hmm wait, but that means for roles-configured setups, a 429 now: entry-1 provider ladder retries up to its budget (with backoff honoring Retry-After) before roles rotate. That changes timing but keeps semantics: rotation still happens, just later. But omp's policy "free credential switch first" would be delayed... And existing roles tests: they test with fake stream functions, not real provider adapters — the FallbackStreamFunction tests inject their own `streamForKey` (which don't include the transient wrapper). So roles tests wouldn't break.

But is it GOOD? A rate-limited key with 3 chain entries: inner ladder burns, say, 3 attempts × backoff (min 2s max 60s each) before failover. With `Retry-After: 60`, that's ~2 minutes wasted before rotating to a working key. Bad for multi-key setups. But the harbor bench scenario (single key, single model) is the primary target.

**Option B (wire the roles engine even for a single model):** Make the CLI wrap the legacy stream in a single-entry FallbackStreamFunction. This gives 429 retries with backoff, honoring Retry-After, plus the last-entry wait-out (`maxWaitForLastEntry`). But: FallbackStreamFunction needs ChainEntry with keyRing and streamForKey; constructing from the legacy path requires plumbing. And it changes a LOT of behavior for single-model users (notices, cooldowns, exhaustion stories). Bigger blast radius. Also the ticket explicitly says "In fa's provider layer".

**Option C (bounded 429 retry in the transient ladder, opt-out when roles exist):** In `providerStreamFunction`, we don't know whether a roles wrapper will sit above. But actually — does it matter? Roles wrapper sits above ONLY when roles resolve. The provider functions are also used directly by compaction smol streams etc.

Let me re-read the ticket's proposed fix:

"In fa's provider layer: classify 429/5xx/timeouts as transient → retry with exponential backoff + jitter (e.g., min 2s, max 60s, honoring Retry-After), bounded by the deadline clock (leave the 120s wrap-up margin intact). 401/403/400 stay fatal."

So the ticket wants the provider-layer ladder to treat 429 like other transient errors — retry in place with backoff, honoring Retry-After, bounded by deadline. The "429_retry event to the session log" for post-mortems.

I think the cleanest fix respecting the architecture:

1. **Add rate-limit handling to the transient ladder** (`transient_retry_stream.dart`): a dedicated rate-limit retry class — the ladder already has maxAttempts and fixed delay; I need exponential backoff + jitter + Retry-After honoring + a bound. When the rate-limit chain exhausts, the terminal carries the exhaustion story that embeds the raw 429 lines → `isRateLimitOrQuota` still matches (the evidence quotes the raw wording) → roles layer above can still rotate/fail over. The exhaustion headline "Provider retry chain exhausted after..." does NOT match `_rateLimitGuardPatterns`? Wait — check: `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` includes `rate.?limit`, `quota`, `\b429\b`... The exhaustion story says "Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 62s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached. Try again later." — that MATCHES `\b429\b` and `rate.?limit`. So `isRateLimitOrQuota` → true. And for `isTransientNetworkError` (the same file's classifier used by... itself): the guard `_rateLimitGuardPatterns.any(...)` returns false → stays non-transient — good, the ladder won't re-retry its own terminal (well, the ladder returns the terminal directly, so it doesn't re-classify anyway; but the roles wrapper's transport classifier checks `isTransientTransportError` which excludes rate-limit patterns AND exhaustion stories → forwards. Then `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota` → true → rotate/failover.

So composition works: provider ladder burns its bounded in-place budget; on exhaustion the roles layer sees a rate-limit-classified terminal and rotates/fails over. Actually wait — but then for multi-key chains, before rotating, we burn the provider-ladder budget. Hmm. Is there a way to keep the old behavior when a roles wrapper is above? The provider ladder can't know its caller... BUT: the ladder's exhaustion keeps roles semantics; and in-place retries with backoff before rotation is EXACTLY what omp's policy does anyway (omp: auto-retry with backoff first, then rotate credentials, then fail over). omp's `#handleRetryableError`: retry same session up to N times with backoff, then credential switch, then model fallback. ## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The

blocks.text:
"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`

Usage:

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached..."). We could make the roles classifier match the rate-limit INSIDE the exhaustion story. Hmm, but issue #1168 explicitly made the exhaustion terminal opaque to prevent re-classification ("treat the signature as terminal - no further retries, no 'not retried' rewrap"). But that's for the transport class. Actually `isTransientExhaustionStory` is excluded from `isTransientTransportError` — but `isRateLimitOrQuota` doesn't check the exhaustion signature; it only matches patterns. So a rate-limit-ladder exhaustion ("Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 60s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...") WOULD match `rate.?limit` patterns via the attempts evidence → `isRateLimitOrQuota` returns true → the roles layer WOULD rotate/fail over. Interesting! That actually composes: the inner ladder does a few quick in-place retries with backoff; on exhaustion, the roles layer sees a rate-limit-shaped terminal and rotates/fails over.

Hmm wait, but that means for roles-configured setups, a 429 now: entry-1 provider ladder retries up to its budget (with backoff honoring Retry-After) before roles rotate. That changes timing but keeps semantics: rotation still happens, just later. But omp's policy "free credential switch first" would be delayed... And existing roles tests: they test with fake stream functions, not real provider adapters — the FallbackStreamFunction tests inject their own `streamForKey` (which don't include the transient wrapper). So roles tests wouldn't break.

But is it GOOD? A rate-limited key with 3 chain entries: inner ladder burns, say, 3 attempts × backoff (min 2s max 60s each) before failover. With `Retry-After: 60`, that's ~2 minutes wasted before rotating to a working key. Bad for multi-key setups. But the harbor bench scenario (single key, single model) is the primary target.

**Option B (wire the roles engine even for a single model):** Make the CLI wrap the legacy stream in a single-entry FallbackStreamFunction. This gives 429 retries with backoff, honoring Retry-After, plus the last-entry wait-out (`maxWaitForLastEntry`). But: FallbackStreamFunction needs ChainEntry with keyRing and streamForKey; constructing from the legacy path requires plumbing. And it changes a LOT of behavior for single-model users (notices, cooldowns, exhaustion stories). Bigger blast radius. Also the ticket explicitly says "In fa's provider layer".

**Option C (bounded 429 retry in the transient ladder, opt-out when roles exist):** In `providerStreamFunction`, we don't know whether a roles wrapper will sit above. But actually — does it matter? Roles wrapper sits above ONLY when roles resolve. The provider functions are also used directly by compaction smol streams etc.

Let me re-read the ticket's proposed fix:

"In fa's provider layer: classify 429/5xx/timeouts as transient → retry with exponential backoff + jitter (e.g., min 2s, max 60s, honoring Retry-After), bounded by the deadline clock (leave the 120s wrap-up margin intact). 401/403/400 stay fatal."

So the ticket wants the provider-layer ladder to treat 429 like other transient errors — retry in place with backoff, honoring Retry-After, bounded by deadline. The "429_retry event to the session log" for post-mortems.

I think the cleanest fix respecting the architecture:

1. **Add rate-limit handling to the transient ladder** (`transient_retry_stream.dart`): a dedicated rate-limit retry class — the ladder already has maxAttempts and fixed delay; I need exponential backoff + jitter + Retry-After honoring + a bound. When the rate-limit chain exhausts, the terminal carries the exhaustion story that embeds the raw 429 lines → `isRateLimitOrQuota` still matches (the evidence quotes the raw wording) → roles layer above can still rotate/fail over. The exhaustion headline "Provider retry chain exhausted after..." does NOT match `_rateLimitGuardPatterns`? Wait — check: `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` includes `rate.?limit`, `quota`, `\b429\b`... The exhaustion story says "Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 62s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached. Try again later." — that MATCHES `\b429\b` and `rate.?limit`. So `isRateLimitOrQuota` → true. And for `isTransientNetworkError` (the same file's classifier used by... itself): the guard `_rateLimitGuardPatterns.any(...)` returns false → stays non-transient — good, the ladder won't re-retry its own terminal (well, the ladder returns the terminal directly, so it doesn't re-classify anyway; but the roles wrapper's transport classifier checks `isTransientTransportError` which excludes rate-limit patterns AND exhaustion stories → forwards. Then `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota` → true → rotate/failover.

So composition works: provider ladder burns its bounded in-place budget; on exhaustion the roles layer sees a rate-limit-classified terminal and rotates/fails over. Actually wait — but then for multi-key chains, before rotating, we burn the provider-ladder budget. Hmm. Is there a way to keep the old behavior when a roles wrapper is above? The provider ladder can't know its caller... BUT: the ladder's exhaustion keeps roles semantics; and in-place retries with backoff before rotation is EXACTLY what omp's policy does anyway (omp: auto-retry with backoff first, then rotate credentials, then fail over). omp's `#handleRetryableError`: retry same session up to N times with backoff, then credential switch, then model fallback. """Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...").
