"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_TOKEN = r"(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])"
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


# ── gh-1576: external-kill audit trail (I2) — signal lifecycle ──────────
# ONE process-level disposition per signal, held on behalf of every live

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached..."). We could make the roles classifier match the rate-limit INSIDE the exhaustion story. Hmm, but issue #1168 explicitly made the exhaustion terminal opaque to prevent re-classification ("treat the signature as terminal - no further retries, no 'not retried' rewrap"). But that's for the transport class. Actually `isTransientExhaustionStory` is excluded from `isTransientTransportError` — but `isRateLimitOrQuota` doesn't check the exhaustion signature; it only matches patterns. So a rate-limit-ladder exhaustion ("Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 60s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...") WOULD match `rate.?limit` patterns via the attempts evidence → `isRateLimitOrQuota` returns true → the roles layer WOULD rotate/fail over. Interesting! That actually composes: the inner ladder does a few quick in-place retries with backoff; on exhaustion, the roles layer sees a rate-limit-shaped terminal and rotates/fails over.

Hmm wait, but that means for roles-configured setups, a 429 now: entry-1 provider ladder retries up to its budget (with backoff honoring Retry-After) before roles rotate. That changes timing but keeps semantics: rotation still happens, just later. But omp's policy "free credential switch first" would be delayed... And existing roles tests: they test with fake stream functions, not real provider adapters — the FallbackStreamFunction tests inject their own `streamForKey` (which don't include the transient wrapper). So roles tests wouldn't break.

But is it GOOD? A rate-limited key with 3 chain entries: inner ladder burns, say, 3 attempts × backoff (min 2s max 60s each) before failover. With `Retry-After: 60`, that's ~2 minutes wasted before rotating to a working key. Bad for multi-key setups. But the harbor bench scenario (single key, single model) is the primary target.

**Option B (wire the roles engine even for a single model):** Make the CLI wrap the legacy stream in a single-entry FallbackStreamFunction. This gives 429 retries with backoff, honoring Retry-After, plus the last-entry wait-out (`maxWaitForLastEntry`). But: FallbackStreamFunction needs ChainEntry with keyRing and streamForKey; constructing from the legacy path requires plumbing. And it changes a LOT of behavior for single-model users (notices, cooldowns, exhaustion stories). Bigger blast radius. Also the ticket explicitly says "In fa's provider layer".

**Option C (bounded 429 retry in the transient ladder, opt-out when roles exist):** In `providerStreamFunction`, we don't know whether a roles wrapper will sit above. But actually — does it matter? Roles wrapper sits above ONLY when roles resolve. The provider functions are also used directly by compaction smol streams etc.

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached..."). We could make the roles classifier match the rate-limit INSIDE the exhaustion story. Hmm, but issue #1168 explicitly made the exhaustion terminal opaque to prevent re-classification ("treat the signature as terminal - no further retries, no 'not retried' rewrap"). But that's for the transport class. Actually `isTransientExhaustionStory` is excluded from `isTransientTransportError` — but `isRateLimitOrQuota` doesn't check the exhaustion signature; it only matches patterns. So a rate-limit-ladder exhaustion ("Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 60s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...") WOULD match `rate.?limit` patterns via the attempts evidence → `isRateLimitOrQuota` returns true → the roles layer WOULD rotate/fail over. Interesting! That actually composes: the inner ladder does a few quick in-place retries with backoff; on exhaustion, the roles layer sees a rate-limit-shaped terminal and rotates/fails over.

Hmm wait, but that means for roles-configured setups, a 429 now: entry-1 provider ladder retries up to its budget (with backoff honoring Retry-After) before roles rotate. That changes timing but keeps semantics: rotation still happens, just later. But omp's policy "free credential switch first" would be delayed... And existing roles tests: they test with fake stream functions, not real provider adapters — the FallbackStreamFunction tests inject their own `streamForKey` (which don't include the transient wrapper). So roles tests wouldn't break.

But is it GOOD? A rate-limited key with 3 chain entries: inner ladder burns, say, 3 attempts × backoff (min 2s max 60s each) before failover. With `Retry-After: 60`, that's ~2 minutes wasted before rotating to a working key. Bad for multi-key setups. But the harbor bench scenario (single key, single model) is the primary target.

**Option B (wire the roles engine even for a single model):** Make the CLI wrap the legacy stream in a single-entry FallbackStreamFunction. This gives 429 retries with backoff, honoring Retry-After, plus the last-entry wait-out (`maxWaitForLastEntry`). But: FallbackStreamFunction needs ChainEntry with keyRing and streamForKey; constructing from the legacy path requires plumbing. And it changes a LOT of behavior for single-model users (notices, cooldowns, exhaustion stories). Bigger blast radius. Also the ticket explicitly says "In fa's provider layer".

**Option C (bounded 429 retry in the transient ladder, opt-out when roles exist):** In `providerStreamFunction`, we don't know whether a roles wrapper will sit above. But actually — does it matter? Roles wrapper sits above ONLY when roles resolve. The provider functions are also used directly by compaction smol streams etc.

Let me re-read the ticket's proposed fix:

"In fa's provider layer: classify 429/5xx/timeouts as transient → retry with exponential backoff + jitter (e.g., min 2s, max 60s, honoring Retry-After), bounded by the deadline clock (leave the 120s wrap-up margin intact). 401/403/400 stay fatal."

So the ticket wants the provider-layer ladder to treat 429 like other transient errors — retry in place with backoff, honoring Retry-After, bounded by deadline. The "429_retry event to the session log" for post-mortems.

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time

from pathlib import Path

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,

    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE

    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [

    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),

    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

# ONE process-level disposition per signal, held on behalf of every live

_AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER: dict = {}


def _previous_restorable(previous) -> bool:
    """False when the captured disposition cannot be restored from here.

    `asyncio.unix_events._sighandler_noop` means ANOTHER loop owns the
    signal via its own add_signal_handler registration — we can neither

    default_int_handler are all restorable via signal.signal.
    """

    noop = getattr(signal, "sighandler_noop", None) or getattr(

    return not (noop is not None and previous is noop)

blocks.text:
"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_TOKEN = r"(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])"
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0

# ── gh-1576: external-kill audit trail (I2) — signal lifecycle ──────────
# ONE process-level disposition per signal, held on behalf of every live
# FaAgent trial in the loop (the workflow exposes --n-concurrent):
# the FIRST trial captures the process's previous disposition and

blocks.text:
"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import fa_agent_timeout as _timeout

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (
    ApiRateLimitError,
    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only
# carries this dir.
_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_TOKEN = r"(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])"
_429_SAME_LINE = (
    r"(?im)^[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*"
    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [
    # Replaces the inherited `rate.?limit` substring entry.
    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),
    # Sibling audit (gh-1592): `too many requests` — same free-text
    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

# Issue #1408 AC1 (review 5456649624): the in-container job-log dir,
# OUTSIDE the graded task workspace — same constant the terminal-bench
# adapter defines (bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py); a future relocation
# must move the two adapters together.
_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR = "/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs"

# Pinned $/Mtok table (data, not code) for est_cost_usd (issue #1123).
_PRICING_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "pricing.json"

# Sessions are written here inside the environment; harbor syncs /logs/agent
# back to the host trial dir after the trial (Trial._download_agent_logs).
_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0
_AUDIT_PATH = "/logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json"


# ── gh-1576: external-kill audit trail (I2) — signal lifecycle ──────────
# ONE process-level disposition per signal, held on behalf of every live
# FaAgent trial in the loop (the workflow exposes --n-concurrent):
# the FIRST trial captures the process's previous disposition and
# installs, overlapping trials attach to the same holder, and the LAST
# release removes the handler and RESTORES the captured disposition.
# (Review round 2, PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6sD_xd: a bare
# loop.remove_signal_handler leaves SIG_DFL behind — the captured
# `previous` (harbor's graceful handler) permanently gone for the rest
# of the process — and per-trial installs clobber each other when
# trials overlap.)
_AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER: dict = {}


def _previous_restorable(previous) -> bool:
    """False when the captured disposition cannot be restored from here.

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`

Usage:

I see the testing pattern. Now, the crucial design question: **how to fix this per the ticket while preserving the roles-layer policy.**

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

**Option A (provider layer 429 retry, bounded):** Modify `transientRetryStreamFunction` to also retry rate-limit errors with backoff (honoring Retry-After, min 2s, max 60s), bounded by a deadline clock. But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. That contradicts the documented architecture and existing tests ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"; roles tests assert rotation happens).

Hmm, wait. Actually, would it? Think: roles wrapper calls provider stream (with transient retry inside). A 429 comes → the inner ladder retries it (with backoff, bounded) → if the retry succeeds, the roles wrapper never knew — fine, the request succeeded on the same entry, no rotation needed. If the inner ladder exhausts (e.g., Retry-After 90s but bound 60s... exhaust after N attempts), the inner pushes the exhaustion terminal "Provider retry chain exhausted after N attempt(s)...". The roles wrapper's `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota(event.error)` — the exhaustion story does NOT match the rate-limit patterns... so it would not rotate/fail over; it would forward verbatim. That breaks the roles policy: with 3 chain entries, a 429 on entry 1 should rotate to entry 2 quickly, not have entry 1 burn its own retry budget.

Unless... the exhaustion terminal preserves the original 429 wording inside ("Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached..."). We could make the roles classifier match the rate-limit INSIDE the exhaustion story. Hmm, but issue #1168 explicitly made the exhaustion terminal opaque to prevent re-classification ("treat the signature as terminal - no further retries, no 'not retried' rewrap"). But that's for the transport class. Actually `isTransientExhaustionStory` is excluded from `isTransientTransportError` — but `isRateLimitOrQuota` doesn't check the exhaustion signature; it only matches patterns. So a rate-limit-ladder exhaustion ("Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 60s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached...") WOULD match `rate.?limit` patterns via the attempts evidence → `isRateLimitOrQuota` returns true → the roles layer WOULD rotate/fail over. Interesting! That actually composes: the inner ladder does a few quick in-place retries with backoff; on exhaustion, the roles layer sees a rate-limit-shaped terminal and rotates/fails over.

Hmm wait, but that means for roles-configured setups, a 429 now: entry-1 provider ladder retries up to its budget (with backoff honoring Retry-After) before roles rotate. That changes timing but keeps semantics: rotation still happens, just later. But omp's policy "free credential switch first" would be delayed... And existing roles tests: they test with fake stream functions, not real provider adapters — the FallbackStreamFunction tests inject their own `streamForKey` (which don't include the transient wrapper). So roles tests wouldn't break.

But is it GOOD? A rate-limited key with 3 chain entries: inner ladder burns, say, 3 attempts × backoff (min 2s max 60s each) before failover. With `Retry-After: 60`, that's ~2 minutes wasted before rotating to a working key. Bad for multi-key setups. But the harbor bench scenario (single key, single model) is the primary target.

**Option B (wire the roles engine even for a single model):** Make the CLI wrap the legacy stream in a single-entry FallbackStreamFunction. This gives 429 retries with backoff, honoring Retry-After, plus the last-entry wait-out (`maxWaitForLastEntry`). But: FallbackStreamFunction needs ChainEntry with keyRing and streamForKey; constructing from the legacy path requires plumbing. And it changes a LOT of behavior for single-model users (notices, cooldowns, exhaustion stories). Bigger blast radius. Also the ticket explicitly says "In fa's provider layer".

**Option C (bounded 429 retry in the transient ladder, opt-out when roles exist):** In `providerStreamFunction`, we don't know whether a roles wrapper will sit above. But actually — does it matter? Roles wrapper sits above ONLY when roles resolve. The provider functions are also used directly by compaction smol streams etc.

Let me re-read the ticket's proposed fix:

"In fa's provider layer: classify 429/5xx/timeouts as transient → retry with exponential backoff + jitter (e.g., min 2s, max 60s, honoring Retry-After), bounded by the deadline clock (leave the 120s wrap-up margin intact). 401/403/400 stay fatal."

So the ticket wants the provider-layer ladder to treat 429 like other transient errors — retry in place with backoff, honoring Retry-After, bounded by deadline. The "429_retry event to the session log" for post-mortems.

I think the cleanest fix respecting the architecture:

1. **Add rate-limit handling to the transient ladder** (`transient_retry_stream.dart`): a dedicated rate-limit retry class — the ladder already has maxAttempts and fixed delay; I need exponential backoff + jitter + Retry-After honoring + a bound. When the rate-limit chain exhausts, the terminal carries the exhaustion story that embeds the raw 429 lines → `isRateLimitOrQuota` still matches (the evidence quotes the raw wording) → roles layer above can still rotate/fail over. The exhaustion headline "Provider retry chain exhausted after..." does NOT match `_rateLimitGuardPatterns`? Wait — check: `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` includes `rate.?limit`, `quota`, `\b429\b`... The exhaustion story says "Provider retry chain exhausted after 3 attempt(s) over 62s — the endpoint kept failing. Attempts: 429: Rate limit reached. Try again later." — that MATCHES `\b429\b` and `rate.?limit`. So `isRateLimitOrQuota` → true. And for `isTransientNetworkError` (the same file's classifier used by... itself): the guard `_rateLimitGuardPatterns.any(...)` returns false → stays non-transient — good, the ladder won't re-retry its own terminal (well, the ladder returns the terminal directly, so it doesn't re-classify anyway; but the roles wrapper's transport classifier checks `isTransientTransportError` which excludes rate-limit patterns AND exhaustion stories → forwards. Then `_nonQueueRetryable` checks `isRateLimitOrQuota` → true → rotate/failover.

So composition works: provider ladder burns its bounded in-place budget; on exhaustion the roles layer sees a rate-limit-classified terminal and rotates/fails over. Actually wait — but then for multi-key chains, before rotating, we burn the provider-ladder budget. Hmm. Is there a way to keep the old behavior when a roles wrapper is above? The provider ladder can't know its caller... BUT: the ladder's exhaustion keeps roles semantics; and in-place retries with backoff before rotation is EXACTLY what omp's policy does anyway (omp: auto-retry with backoff first, then rotate credentials, then fail over). omp's `#handleRetryableError`: retry same session up to N times with backoff, then credential switch, then model fallback. """Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

import base64
import json
import os

import sys

import time

# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output

    """False when the captured disposition cannot be restored from here.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A single provider `429 Rate limit reached` kills the whole fa run (exit 1) mid-trial, scoring 0 reward for bench work already in progress — 5 of 30 trials in run 7 died this way with `n_retries: 0`.

**Root cause**: The provider-layer retry ladder (`lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`, `transientRetryStreamFunction` wrapped around every adapter by `providerStreamFunction` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart`) classifies retryable failures via `isTransientNetworkError`, whose `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` deliberately EXCLUDE rate limits ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"). The roles layer that owns 429s (`FallbackStreamFunction` in `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`) is only wired when a model-roles chain resolves (`agent_cli.dart`: `resolveRole(defaultModelRole) != null` → `applyToAgent`). The harbor bench runs a single provider/model with no roles chain, so a 429 travels the ladder un-retried, surfaces as the raw `429: Rate limit reached...` error event, the run ends with exit 1 and `ApiRateLimitError` — nobody owns the 429 in the no-roles configuration.

**Impact**: On long bench shards a single transient quota blip converts a likely-pass trial into a certain fail (run 7: make-doom-for-mips killed after 16 requests/733K tokens; merge-diff-arc-agi-task after ONE request; 3 of the 5 were 4/5 near-misses).

**Fix approach**: Give the 429 class an in-place retry policy in the provider ladder (the layer every configuration shares): a pre-commit rate-limit error is replayed with exponential backoff + jitter (base 2s, cap 60s, honoring the parsed `Retry-After`), bounded by (a) its own attempt budget and (b) the session deadline clock minus a wrap-up margin (default 120s, matching the harbor adapter's `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s` contract) so a retry never eats the wrap-up window. Budget/spending exhaustion (`insufficient_quota` family, issue #926) stays terminal; 401/403/400 stay fatal; post-commit (mid-answer) 429s still stand (a replay would duplicate the transcript). The exhaustion terminal embeds the raw per-attempt 429 lines, so upstream consumers keep classifying the verdict as rate-limit: the roles layer's `isRateLimitOrQuota` still rotates/fails over when a chain IS configured, and harbor's anchored classifier still sees `429 … rate limit` on one line. Each retry is announced through the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook; the CLI classifies the notice and appends a `429_retry` custom record to the session JSONL for post-mortems.

**Previous attempt**: None — first fix for gh-1602 (run 7 was the first shard with the gh-1592 classifier, which made the 429 deaths visible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import shlex

import sys

import time

)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error

# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429

# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every

# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —

# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,

# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.

_429_TOKEN = r"(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])"

    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [

    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

Key insight from the ticket's evidence: the harbor bench runs a single provider with no roles chain. `providerStreamFunction` wraps the adapter with `transientRetryStreamFunction`, which deliberately does NOT retry rate limits — so a 429 kills the call.

The roles layer handles 429s — but only when configured. The gap: **when no roles chain is configured, nobody owns the 429.**

Design options:

But this breaks the roles policy: the roles ladder above would never see the 429 → no key rotation, no failover to other chain entries. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A single provider `429 Rate limit reached` kills the whole fa run (exit 1) mid-trial, scoring 0 reward for bench work already in progress — 5 of 30 trials in run 7 died this way with `n_retries: 0`.

**Root cause**: The provider-layer retry ladder (`lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`, `transientRetryStreamFunction` wrapped around every adapter by `providerStreamFunction` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart`) classifies retryable failures via `isTransientNetworkError`, whose `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` deliberately EXCLUDE rate limits ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"). The roles layer that owns 429s (`FallbackStreamFunction` in `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`) is only wired when a model-roles chain resolves (`agent_cli.dart`: `resolveRole(defaultModelRole) != null` → `applyToAgent`). The harbor bench runs a single provider/model with no roles chain, so a 429 travels the ladder un-retried, surfaces as the raw `429: Rate limit reached...` error event, the run ends with exit 1 and `ApiRateLimitError` — nobody owns the 429 in the no-roles configuration.

**Impact**: On long bench shards a single transient quota blip converts a likely-pass trial into a certain fail (run 7: make-doom-for-mips killed after 16 requests/733K tokens; merge-diff-arc-agi-task after ONE request; 3 of the 5 were 4/5 near-misses).

**Fix approach**: Give the 429 class an in-place retry policy in the provider ladder (the layer every configuration shares): a pre-commit rate-limit error is replayed with exponential backoff + jitter (base 2s, cap 60s, honoring the parsed `Retry-After`), bounded by (a) its own attempt budget and (b) the session deadline clock minus a wrap-up margin (default 120s, matching the harbor adapter's `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s` contract) so a retry never eats the wrap-up window. Budget/spending exhaustion (`insufficient_quota` family, issue #926) stays terminal; 401/403/400 stay fatal; post-commit (mid-answer) 429s still stand (a replay would duplicate the transcript). The exhaustion terminal embeds the raw per-attempt 429 lines, so upstream consumers keep classifying the verdict as rate-limit: the roles layer's `isRateLimitOrQuota` still rotates/fails over when a chain IS configured, and harbor's anchored classifier still sees `429 … rate limit` on one line. Each retry is announced through the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook; the CLI classifies the notice and appends a `429_retry` custom record to the session JSONL for post-mortems.

**Previous attempt**: None — first fix for gh-1602 (run 7 was the first shard with the gh-1592 classifier, which made the 429 deaths visible).

"""Harbor adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Same shape as the shipped cline-cli adapter: a BaseInstalledAgent that
uploads the `dart build cli` bundle into the task environment, installs it
to /opt/fa, and runs `fa -p "<instruction>"` as the environment's agent
user, so fa's bash/read/write tools operate on the container filesystem.
Reuses the legacy env-provider-preconfig contract from
bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py:

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah),
                         uploaded and extracted to /opt/fa by install().
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122): same env contract as
  bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py (shared bench/fa_agent_timeout.py) —
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER. With any knob set, run() supervises the fa
  exec under the progress-aware ladder (progress = growth of
  /logs/agent/fa.txt, the tee'd agent output that already exists) and
  kills + reports an asyncio.TimeoutError (harbor's native
  AgentTimeoutError classification) on stall or hard ceiling; the audit
  trail lands in /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json, synced back with
  the other agent logs. No knobs set => today's single awaited exec.

  Round 3 (gh-1556, harbor parity for #1392/#1430): when a watch knob is
  set (FA_STALL_GAP_SEC / FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC — bench-harbor.yml
  sets both on every shard, so progress-watch is the bench default), the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch, not the byte-growth
  ladder; a stall/ceiling kill also exports FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS to fa
  (effective cap minus a 120s wrap-up margin) so fa can land partial
  results before the guillotine. The kill path uses the `[f]a` bracket
  trick: the pre-fix self-matching `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'`
  SIGTERMed the exec wrapper's own shell (exit 143 skipped the audit AND
  the TimeoutError, classifying ladder kills as agent crashes) — and the
  kill is wrapped so its failure can never replace the TimeoutError.

Usage:
  PYTHONPATH=bench/harbor_fa harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0 \
    -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e docker -m glm-5.3-flash
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path

from harbor.agents.installed.base import (

    BaseInstalledAgent,
    ErrorPattern,
)
from harbor.environments.base import BaseEnvironment
from harbor.models.agent.context import AgentContext

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only

    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

_VERSION = "0.1.0"

# gh-1592: harbor's failed-command classifier (_classify_exec_error) scans
# a failed exec's stdout+stderr with ERROR_PATTERNS, and its ApiRateLimit
# entries are UNANCHORED substrings — `rate.?limit` matched the tee'd fa
# output of run 38271607849 (shard fa-2.1-docker-cpu-5, trial
# gpt2-codegolf__pKKQfqj) after the 900s timeout kill: the output
# legitimately contains the words "rate limit" (echoed provider-error
# text, fa's own `[roles] rate limited on … — retrying` notices), so the
# failed launch exec surfaced as ApiRateLimitError with no provider 429
# anywhere. The anchor below requires the structured provider-error
# context: `429` and the wording must share ONE line — the shape every
# real 429 reaches fa's output in (`formatProviderError` renders
# `<statusCode>: <message>`, raw HTTP status lines are `HTTP/1.1 429 …`,
# JSON error bodies carry the `"code": 429` inline on one line), while
# fa's own notice lines and echoed prose carry no 429 on the line.
# The token itself is guarded against digit/dot adjacency —
# `(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])` (gh-1592 review): `\b429\b` still matched the
# `429` inside decimals like `0.429` / `429.5` (`.` is a non-word char,
# so both sides of the token were boundaries), letting echoed output that
# pairs a decimal with rate-limit wording re-trigger the
# misclassification; the lookarounds keep every real shape (`429: …`,
# `HTTP/1.1 429 …`, `"code": 429`) while rejecting `0.429`, `429.5`,
# `1429`.
# `(?im)` rides the pattern because harbor compiles with re.IGNORECASE
# only; the `^` anchors each attempt to a line start so classification
# stays linear over multi-MB tee'd streams, and the `[^\r\n]*` spans keep
# every match line-scoped.
_429_TOKEN = r"(?<![\d.])429(?![\d.])"

    r"|^[^\r\n]*{word}[^\r\n]*" + _429_TOKEN + r"[^\r\n]*"
)
_ANCHORED_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS = [

    ErrorPattern(_429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"rate.?limit"), ApiRateLimitError),

    # substring class, anchored the same way. The usage-limit, auth,
    # capacity and safety entries are full-sentence signatures with no
    # observed FP class and stay inherited verbatim.
    ErrorPattern(
        _429_SAME_LINE.format(word=r"too many requests"), ApiRateLimitError
    ),
]

_SESSION_ROOT = "/logs/agent/fah-sessions"

_POLL_SEC = 5.0

# ONE process-level disposition per signal, held on behalf of every live

_AUDIT_SIGNAL_HOLDER: dict = {}


def _previous_restorable(previous) -> bool:
    """False when the captured disposition cannot be restored from here.

    `asyncio.unix_events._sighandler_noop` means ANOTHER loop owns the
    signal via its own add_signal_handler registration — we can neither
    re-register their callback nor faithfully restore it, so we prefer
    NOT installing over half-restoring (the cancel-path flush still
    covers I2). Python-level callables, SIG_DFL, SIG_IGN and
    default_int_handler are all restorable via signal.signal.
    """
    unix_events = getattr(asyncio, "unix_events", None)
    noop = getattr(signal, "sighandler_noop", None) or getattr(

    )
    return not (noop is not None and previous is noop)

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A single provider `429 Rate limit reached` kills the whole fa run (exit 1) mid-trial, scoring 0 reward for bench work already in progress — 5 of 30 trials in run 7 died this way with `n_retries: 0`.

**Root cause**: The provider-layer retry ladder (`lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`, `transientRetryStreamFunction` wrapped around every adapter by `providerStreamFunction` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_catalog.dart`) classifies retryable failures via `isTransientNetworkError`, whose `_rateLimitGuardPatterns` deliberately EXCLUDE rate limits ("rate limits stay with the roles layer"). The roles layer that owns 429s (`FallbackStreamFunction` in `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart`) is only wired when a model-roles chain resolves (`agent_cli.dart`: `resolveRole(defaultModelRole) != null` → `applyToAgent`). The harbor bench runs a single provider/model with no roles chain, so a 429 travels the ladder un-retried, surfaces as the raw `429: Rate limit reached...` error event, the run ends with exit 1 and `ApiRateLimitError` — nobody owns the 429 in the no-roles configuration.

**Impact**: On long bench shards a single transient quota blip converts a likely-pass trial into a certain fail (run 7: make-doom-for-mips killed after 16 requests/733K tokens; merge-diff-arc-agi-task after ONE request; 3 of the 5 were 4/5 near-misses).

**Fix approach**: Give the 429 class an in-place retry policy in the provider ladder (the layer every configuration shares): a pre-commit rate-limit error is replayed with exponential backoff + jitter (base 2s, cap 60s, honoring the parsed `Retry-After`), bounded by (a) its own attempt budget and (b) the session deadline clock minus a wrap-up margin (default 120s, matching the harbor adapter's `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s` contract) so a retry never eats the wrap-up window. Budget/spending exhaustion (`insufficient_quota` family, issue #926) stays terminal; 401/403/400 stay fatal; post-commit (mid-answer) 429s still stand (a replay would duplicate the transcript). The exhaustion terminal embeds the raw per-attempt 429 lines, so upstream consumers keep classifying the verdict as rate-limit: the roles layer's `isRateLimitOrQuota` still rotates/fails over when a chain IS configured, and harbor's anchored classifier still sees `429 … rate limit` on one line. Each retry is announced through the existing `transientRetryNotice` hook; the CLI classifies the notice and appends a `429_retry` custom record to the session JSONL for post-mortems.

**Previous attempt**: None — first fix for gh-1602 (run 7 was the first shard with the gh-1592 classifier, which made the 429 deaths visible).
